idiom_name: encoding/json struct binding: unmatched keys dropped, absent fields keep zero values (json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields is the opt-in strictness)
implementation_notes: encoding/json is part of the standard library and is tolerant by construction: Unmarshal matches object keys against the struct's fields and tags, ignores everything it cannot match, and leaves fields that were not present at their current value, so a struct that declares only the consumed subset is already a tolerant reader. When strictness is wanted (contract tests, internal payloads) the same package offers the explicit opt-in Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields(); when the payload is protobuf rather than JSON, generated messages additionally preserve unknown wire fields, which extends tolerance to binary forward compatibility. Prefer a typed struct over map[string]any for anything sizeable: the struct documents the consumed subset and skips the rest without allocation.
pitfalls: For non-pointer fields, absent and zero are indistinguishable: use *T, json.RawMessage or an explicit map when "not sent" must be told apart from "sent as zero".
Field matching is case-insensitive (JSON "Total" binds to tag `total`), so a case-only rename keeps working while a real rename silently binds nothing at all.

json.Decoder.DisallowUnknownFields turns the reader strict for the whole stream: enabling it in production couples the consumer to the producer's exact schema and defeats the pattern during a partial rollout.
